title: Calculus II: Integration, Series & Applications
description: Advanced integration, applications of accumulation, sequences and series, and power-series approximations for quantitative science.

modifications: Corrected the geometric-series tail arithmetic; the original approximation and exact sum are preserved.

outcomes.description: Select and justify an integration method.
Set up integrals for work, area, and volume.
Use Taylor approximations with an error interpretation.

lesson_objectives.description: Choose substitution, parts, or partial fractions from structure.
Determine whether an improper integral converges.
Select a convergence test for a series.
Use Taylor polynomials with a remainder interpretation.
Set bounds from the physical process before integrating.
Interpret a variable-force integral and check units.
Build a Taylor polynomial from derivatives at a center.
State where a series converges and how truncation error is controlled.
Set up and evaluate the definite integral of a rate model to obtain a total accumulated amount.
Apply the trapezoidal and Simpson's rules to sampled rate data and bound the trapezoidal error using the second derivative.
Evaluate an improper integral of a decaying rate, test its convergence and interpret the finite total.
Construct first- and second-order Taylor polynomials of standard functions about a point.
Bound the approximation error with the Lagrange remainder and compare it with the actual error.
Decide whether a linearization used in a scientific formula is accurate enough for a stated tolerance.

lessons.title: Integration techniques and improper integrals
lessons.worked_example: For C(t)=C₀e^(−kt), k>0, the total exposure is ∫₀∞C₀e^(−kt)dt = C₀/k.

lessons.title: Sequences, series, and approximation error
lessons.worked_example: For |x|<1, 1/(1−x)=Σxⁿ. At x=0.2, truncating after n=2 gives 1.24 versus 1.25; the tail is 0.2³/(1−0.2)=0.008/0.8=0.01.

modules.title: Applications of integration: work and accumulation

lessons.title: Applications of integration: work and accumulation
lessons.worked_example: If a spring-like actuator applies F(x)=4x N from x=0 to 3 m, W=∫₀³4x dx=18 J.

lessons.title: Power series and Taylor error
lessons.worked_example: For eˣ near x=0, the quadratic approximation at x=0.2 is 1+0.2+0.2²/2=1.22; the cubic remainder is under about 0.0017 on that interval.

lessons.title: Integrals as accumulation: total consumption from rate data, numerical rules with error bounds and improper integrals
lessons.worked_example: The exact total of 0.5e^(0.03t) over 0 to 48 h is 53.68 mmol; 12 h samples give a trapezoidal 54.26 (bound 1.09) and Simpson 53.68 mmol; a release rate 2.0e^(−0.1t) totals 20 μg over all time.

lessons.title: Taylor approximations with an error bound: when "approximately" is good enough
lessons.worked_example: At x = 0.2, P₂ for e^(−x) is 0.8200 against 0.8187, within the remainder bound 0.001333; linear decay overstates loss by 2.5% at kt = 0.05; 1 − kt stays within 0.01 of e^(−kt) for kt ≤ 0.141.
